decisions: No new directory: both modules land beside their source in the existing src/calculator/champions package, so packages is empty.

Direction inverted against the roster, which moves the readers out and keeps the vocabulary as the residue leaf. extract_modules.py refuses that: module_survey.py reading COVERAGE_CHANNELS, ChampionModuleContract, DeclarationSites and six more names left in the residue is nine back-edges. Only the leaf can move, so the vocabulary is what moves.

Three modules, not two. Moving the vocabulary alone leaves a 501-line residue, which is still the size arm the split is meant to clear. Splitting the residue again along the line the roster already drew gives contract_vocabulary.py the words, module_survey.py the declaration readers, and module_contract.py the one constructor its six readers already import from, so contract_from_module retargets nowhere.

The champions-to-engine edge the roster wanted still dies: CC_PER_PART is read by _module_cc, which lands in module_survey.py, so contract_vocabulary.py imports nothing from the parser side and the 40 champion modules that want only the coverage words stop pulling it.

Run engine.json before this assignment. extract_modules.py copies the source's own import spelling, so module_contract.py's `from .engine import CC_PER_PART` needs to already read `from .slot_cc import CC_PER_PART` for module_survey.py to land on the leaf.

modules.docstring: The coverage words a champion module declares, and the contract they read into.
Reads each contract fact off a module's three declaration sites and refuses a malformed one.
